food_name: Kolovi olive fruit, sample 1 (Olea europaea L.)
geographical_origin: Lesvos Island, Greece; two olive groves
synonym_source: Martakos et al. 2021; DOI 10.3390/molecules26237182; PubChem CID 5281544
mapping_review_rationale: Exact Stage B parent analyte Oleuropein; source separately quantified oleuropein using an authentic standard, distinct from oleuropein aglycone. Match is exact. Values remain on the reported freeze-dried olive-fruit basis.
mapping_review_source: Martakos et al. 2021; DOI 10.3390/molecules26237182; PubChem CID 5281544
analytical_method: UPLC-HRMS target screening; calibration with authentic reference standard
extraction_method: Pitted fruit freeze-dried, homogenized; methanol extraction and optimized cleanup/SPE; Methods §§3.2–3.3
sample_size: One of seven olive fruit samples (Sample 1)
source_title: Development of Analytical Strategies for the Determination of Olive Fruit Bioactive Compounds Using UPLC-HRMS and HPLC-DAD. Chemical Characterization of Kolovi Lesvos Variety as a Case Study
database_reference: Table 1 (Target screening results), oleuropein row, Sample 1; reported mg/kg
extraction_notes: Table 1 lists oleuropein separately from oleuropein aglycone and related degradation products. Sample 1 reported value is 811 mg/kg. Fruit samples were freeze-dried before analysis; no fresh-weight conversion is attempted.
uncertainty_notes: Across seven samples the range is 3.5–855 mg/kg; authors attribute variation to maturity stage. Values are on the freeze-dried sample basis and should not be compared directly with fresh-weight composition without moisture data.
